bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷二十四 梁書24: 列傳14 李珽 盧曾 孫騭 張俊 張衍 杜荀鶴 羅隱 仇殷 段深
title.en: Volume 24 Book of Later Liang 24: Biographies 14 - Li Ting, Lu Ceng, Sun Zhi, Zhang Jun, Zhang Yan, Du Xunhe, Luo Yin, Chou Yin, Duan Shen
title.raw: 卷二十四 梁書24: 列傳14 李珽 盧曾 孫騭 張俊 張衍 杜荀鶴 羅隱 仇殷 段深 Volume 24 Book of Later Liang 24: Biographies 14 - Li Ting, Lu Ceng, Sun Zhi, Zhang Jun, Zhang Yan, Du Xunhe, Luo Yin, Chou Yin, Duan Shen

sentences.zh: 李珽，字公度，隴西敦煌人。

translations.literal: Li Ting, style Gongdu, a man of Dunhuang in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting, styled Gongdu, came from Dunhuang in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 五世祖忠懿公憕，有大節，見《唐史》。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Duke of Loyal Benevolence Cheng had great integrity; see the 《History of Tang》.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor, Duke of Loyal Benevolence Cheng, was a man of great principle, as recorded in the 《History of Tang》.

sentences.zh: 父縠，仕懿、僖朝，官至右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His father Gu served in the Yi and Xi reigns and rose to Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu had served under Emperors Yizong and Xizong and reached the post of Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 珽聰悟，有才學，尤工詞賦。

translations.literal: Ting was sharp-witted, learned, and especially skilled at lyric prose.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was quick-minded, widely read, and especially gifted at rhapsodies and fu.

sentences.zh: 僖宗朝，晉公王鐸提兵柄，鎮滑台，縠居賓席，鐸見珽，大賞歎之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xizong's reign Duke of Jin Wang Duo held military authority and governed Huatai; Gu sat among his guests; Duo met Ting and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During Xizong's reign Duke of Jin Wang Duo held the armies at Huatai; Gu was among his retainers; when Duo met Ting he admired him greatly.

sentences.zh: 年二十四登進士第，解褐授校書郎，拜監察御史，俄丁內艱。

translations.literal: At twenty-four he passed the jinshi examination, left the robe for collating clerk, was appointed investigating censor, and soon mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he passed the jinshi, entered service as collating clerk, became investigating censor, and soon entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 先是，父旅殯在遠，家貧無以襄事，與弟琪當臘雪以單縗扶杖，銜哀告人，由是兩克遷祔。

translations.literal: Earlier his father's body lay in burial far away; the family was poor and could not afford the funeral; with his brother Qi, in midwinter snow, in plain hemp mourning garments and leaning on staffs, they grieved and begged people, and thereby managed to relocate both for joint enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: His father's coffin had long lain far from home and the family was too poor to bury him properly; Ting and his brother Qi, in deep winter snow, wore plain hemp mourning and leaned on staffs as they went begging in grief until they could bring both parents home for joint burial.

sentences.zh: 而珽日不過食一溢，恒羸臥喪廬中不能興。

translations.literal: Yet Ting ate no more than one dipper a day, constantly emaciated lying in the mourning hut unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Ting ate barely a dipper of food a day, grew gaunt, and for long stretches could not leave the mourning hut.

sentences.zh: 大為時賢所歎。

translations.literal: Greatly admired by the worthies of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the age greatly admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 憂闋，再征為御史，以瘠不起。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was again summoned as censor but was too emaciated to take office.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned again as censor but was too frail to serve.

sentences.zh: 成汭之鎮荊州，辟為掌書記，逾時乃就。

translations.literal: When Cheng Yan governed Jingzhou he recruited him as chief clerk; only after some time did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Yan took Jingzhou he made Ting his chief secretary; Ting delayed some time before accepting.

sentences.zh: 天復中，淮寇大舉圍夏口，逼巴陵，太祖患之，飛命成汭率水軍十萬援於鄂。

translations.literal: In Tianfu, Huai raiders in force besieged Xiakou and pressed Baling; the Founder was anxious and sent urgent orders for Cheng Yan to lead a hundred thousand naval troops to aid Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu Huai forces besieged Xiakou and threatened Baling; the Founder was alarmed and ordered Cheng Yan post-haste to Ezhou with a hundred thousand sailors.

sentences.zh: 珽入言曰：「今舳艫容介士千人，載稻倍之，緩急不可動。

translations.literal: Ting entered and said: "Now each warship holds a thousand armored men and carries twice as much rice; it cannot move flexibly in urgent or slack moments.
translations.idiomatic: Ting advised him: "Each ship now carries a thousand fighting men and twice as much grain—it cannot maneuver when speed matters.

sentences.zh: 吳人剽輕，若為所絆，則武陵、武安皆我之仇也，將有後慮；

translations.literal: The Wu men are swift and light; if entangled by them, Wuling and Wu'an will all be our enemies, and there will be future worry;
translations.idiomatic: The Wu are quick and light; if they pin you down, Wuling and Wu'an become our enemies and the rear is exposed;

sentences.zh: 不如遣驍將屯巴陵，大軍對岸，一日不與戰，則吳寇糧絕，而鄂州圍解矣。

translations.literal: better to send bold generals to hold Baling, the main army on the opposite bank; if for one day they do not fight, the Wu raiders' grain will run out and the siege of Ezhou will be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: better to post bold officers at Baling and keep the main fleet on the far bank—one day without battle and the Wu run out of grain and Ezhou is saved.

sentences.zh: 」汭性剛決，不聽。

translations.literal: " Cheng's nature was stubborn and decisive; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng was stubborn and would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 淮人果乘風縱火，舟盡焚，兵盡溺，汭亦自沈於江，朗人、潭人遂入荊渚，一如所料。

translations.literal: The Huai men indeed rode the wind to set fire; all boats burned, all soldiers drowned; Cheng also drowned himself in the river; men of Lang and Tan then entered the Jing region—just as forecast.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai did ride the wind to burn the fleet; every ship was lost and every man drowned; Cheng drowned himself in the river; Lang and Tan troops then overran Jing—exactly as Ting had foretold.

sentences.zh: 未幾，襄帥趙匡凝復奏為掌記，入為左補闕。

translations.literal: Before long Xiang commander Zhao Kuangning again recommended him as chief recorder; he entered court as Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xiang commander Zhao Kuangning again named him chief recorder; he entered court as Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 又明年，太祖為元帥，以襄陽貳於己，率兵擊破之，趙匡凝奔揚州，太祖復署珽為天平軍掌書記。

translations.literal: The next year the Founder as commander-in-chief, because Xiangyang was disloyal, led troops to defeat it; Zhao Kuangning fled to Yangzhou; the Founder again appointed Ting chief clerk of the Tianping army.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as commander-in-chief, the Founder attacked disloyal Xiangyang, broke it, and drove Zhao Kuangning to Yangzhou; he again made Ting secretary of the Tianping army.

sentences.zh: 一日，大會將佐，指珽曰：「此真書記也。」

translations.literal: One day at a great meeting of officers he pointed to Ting and said: "This is the true secretary."
translations.idiomatic: One day at a council of officers he pointed to Ting and said, "There is a real secretary."

sentences.zh: 滄州節度使劉守文拒命，太祖引兵十餘萬圍之，久而未下，乃召珽草檄。

translations.literal: Cangzhou commissioner Liu Shouwen defied orders; the Founder led more than a hundred thousand troops to besiege him; long unable to take it, he summoned Ting to draft a proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangzhou commissioner Liu Shouwen rebelled the Founder besieged him with more than a hundred thousand men; the city held for long months, and he called on Ting to draft the assault proclamation.

sentences.zh: 珽即就外次，筆不停綴，登時而成，大為太祖嗟賞。

translations.literal: Ting at once went to an outer station, his brush never pausing, finished in the moment, and greatly won the Founder's admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Ting stepped to a side room and wrote without pause; the draft was done at once and the Founder marveled.

sentences.zh: 受禪之歲，宰臣除為考功員外郎、知制誥，珽揣太祖未欲首以舊僚超拜清顯，三上章固辭，優詔褒允，尋以本官監曹州事。

translations.literal: The year of receiving the mandate, the chief ministers appointed him Acting Director of Examination, outer rank, and drafter of edicts; Ting guessed the Founder was unwilling to be the first to advance an old subordinate to a lofty clear post, thrice submitted memorials firmly declining, a gracious edict praised and granted it, and soon with his original office he supervised Cao prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of the Founder's enthronement the chief ministers made him Acting Director of Examination and edict drafter; Ting sensed the Founder was loath to promote an old follower straight to a lofty post, declined three times in memorials, received a gracious edict of praise, and soon supervised Cao with his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 曹去京數舍，吏民豪猾，前後十餘政，未有善罷者。

translations.literal: Cao was several post-stages from the capital; officials and people were powerful and crafty; more than ten predecessors in office, none had ended well.
translations.idiomatic: Cao lay several stages from the capital; its officials and gentry were fierce; more than ten predecessors had left the post in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 珽在任期歲，眾庶以寧。

translations.literal: Ting served one year in term; the multitude was thereby at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In one year under Ting the people were calm.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部郎中、崇政院學士。

translations.literal: He entered court as Bureau Director in the Ministry of War and Academic in the Court for Upholding Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Bureau Director in the Ministry of War and academician of the Court for Upholding Governance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以許帥馮行襲疾甚，出為許州留後。

translations.literal: Before long, because Xu commander Feng Xingxi was gravely ill, he went out as Xu prefecture acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because Xu commander Feng Xingxi was gravely ill, he was sent out as acting governor of Xu.

sentences.zh: 先是，行襲有牙兵二千，皆蔡人也，太祖深以為憂，乃遣珽馳往，以伺察之。

translations.literal: Earlier Xingxi had two thousand guard troops, all men of Cai; the Founder deeply worried and sent Ting post-haste to observe them.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi still had two thousand guard troops, all Cai men; the Founder was deeply uneasy and sent Ting post-haste to watch the situation.

sentences.zh: 珽至傳舍，召將吏親加撫慰。

translations.literal: Ting reached the relay station, summoned officers and clerks, and personally added consolation.
translations.idiomatic: At the relay station Ting summoned the officers and comforted them in person.

sentences.zh: 行襲欲使人代受詔，珽曰：「東首加朝服，禮也。

translations.literal: Xingxi wished to have someone receive the edict in his place; Ting said: "Facing east and putting on court dress is the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi wanted a proxy to receive the edict; Ting said, "To face east in court dress is the proper rite.

sentences.zh: 」乃於臥內宣詔，令善自補養，苟有不諱，子孫俱保後福。

translations.literal: " He then proclaimed the edict within the sickbed chamber, ordering him to nourish himself well; if there should be misfortune, his sons and grandsons would all secure later blessing.
translations.idiomatic: " He read the edict at the bedside, urging him to recover; should the worst come, his sons and grandsons would still enjoy lasting favor.

sentences.zh: 行襲泣謝，遂解二印以授珽，代掌軍府事。

translations.literal: Xingxi wept in thanks, then relinquished two seals to give to Ting, who acted in charge of military headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi wept his thanks and handed Ting both seals to run the headquarters in his stead.

sentences.zh: 太祖覽奏曰：「予固知珽必辦吾事，行襲門戶不朽矣。

translations.literal: The Founder reading the memorial said: "I knew indeed Ting would accomplish my affair; Xingxi's house will not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the report, the Founder said, "I knew Ting would handle this for me—Xingxi's line will endure.

sentences.zh: 」乃以珽為匡國軍留後，尋征為左諫議大夫兼宣徽副使。

translations.literal: " He then made Ting acting governor of Kuangguo army; soon he was summoned as Left Remonstrance Grand Master and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Ting acting governor of Kuangguo, then recalled him as Left Remonstrance Grand Master and Vice Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從征至魏縣，過內黃，因侍立於行廄，太祖顧曰：「此何故名內黃？

translations.literal: On campaign he reached Wei county, passed Neihuang, and as he attended standing at the traveling stable the Founder turned and said: "Why is this called Neihuang?
translations.idiomatic: On campaign at Wei county he passed Neihuang; while attending the Founder at the traveling stable the Founder asked, "Why is this place called Neihuang?

sentences.zh: 」珽曰：「河南有外黃、小黃，故此有內黃。

translations.literal: " Ting said: "South of the River there are Waihuang and Xiaohuang, hence here is Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: " Ting said, "South of the River are Waihuang and Xiaohuang, so this is Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「在何處？

translations.literal: " He also said: "Where are they?
translations.idiomatic: " The Founder asked, "Where were those?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「秦有外黃都尉，理外黃，有故墉，今在雍丘。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Qin had a Waihuang commandant administering Waihuang; there is an old wall, now at Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Qin had a Waihuang commandant; the old rampart is at Yongqiu today.

sentences.zh: 小黃為高齊所廢，其故墉今在陳留。

translations.literal: Xiaohuang was abolished by Northern Qi; its old wall is now at Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohuang was abolished under Northern Qi; its old site is at Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 」太祖稱獎數四。

translations.literal: " The Founder praised him several times.
translations.idiomatic: " The Founder praised him again and again.

sentences.zh: 及庶人友珪篡位，除右散騎常侍，充侍講學士。

translations.literal: When the commoner Yougui usurped the throne, he was appointed Right Regular Cavalry Attendant and served as lecturer attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the commoner Yougui seized the throne, Ting was made Right Regular Cavalry Attendant and lecturer attendant.

sentences.zh: 內討之日，軍士大擾，珽其夕為亂兵所傷，卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: On the day of inner punitive action the soldiers were greatly disturbed; that evening Ting was wounded by disorderly troops and died in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the inner punitive campaign the army rioted; that night disorderly soldiers wounded Ting, and he died in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 珽性孝友，與弟琪有敦睦之愛，為搢紳所稱。

translations.literal: Ting's nature was filial and fraternal; with his brother Qi he had affection of close harmony, praised by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was filial and brotherly; he and his brother Qi were deeply devoted, and the gentry praised them.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （案：《歐陽史》有《裴迪》、《韋震傳》，今原文已佚，無可采補。）〉

translations.literal: (Comment: the 《Ouyang History》 has biographies of Pei Di and Wei Zhen; the original text here is lost and nothing can be gathered to supplement it.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Ouyang History》 contains biographies of Pei Di and Wei Zhen; the original passage is lost and cannot be restored.)〉

sentences.zh: 盧曾，字孝伯，其先范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Ceng, style Xiaobo, his ancestors were men of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ceng, styled Xiaobo, was of Fanyang descent.

sentences.zh: 頗好書，有所執守。

translations.literal: He rather loved books and had principles he upheld.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and held firm convictions.

sentences.zh: 始為齊州防禦使朱瓊從事，瓊降，預其謀，與之皆來。

translations.literal: At first he was staff officer to Qizhou defense commissioner Zhu Qiong; when Qiong surrendered he took part in the plot and came with him.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Qizhou defense commissioner Zhu Qiong; when Qiong surrendered he helped plan it and came over with him.

sentences.zh: 瓊沒，太祖辟為宣義幕職。

translations.literal: When Qiong died the Founder recruited him to Xuanyi staff office.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiong died the Founder took him onto the Xuanyi staff.

sentences.zh: 曾性忠狷，好貢直，又不能取容於眾，每勳府宴語稍洽，曾率然糾正，輒又忤旨。

translations.literal: Ceng's nature was loyal and blunt, fond of candid remonstrance, yet unable to win acceptance from the multitude; whenever the merit princes' mansion banquets grew pleasant, Ceng would abruptly correct them and again offend the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng was loyal and blunt, given to straight talk, and ill at ease in company; whenever princes of merit were at ease in banquet talk, he would suddenly correct them and give offense again.

sentences.zh: 左長直軍使劉捍委任方重，曾亦不能平。

translations.literal: Left long-direct army commissioner Liu Kan's delegated power was then heavy; Ceng also could not get along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Left long-direct army commissioner Liu Kan was then in full favor; Ceng could not abide him either.

sentences.zh: 冀王友謙初定陝府，命曾往議事，有使院小將從行，嗜酒，荒逸過度。

translations.literal: When Prince of Ji Youqian first secured Shan prefecture he ordered Ceng to go discuss affairs; a minor general of the envoy office accompanied him, fond of wine, dissolute beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Ji Youqian first secured Shanzhou he sent Ceng to negotiate; a minor officer of the envoy bureau went with him, a drunkard and utterly dissolute.

sentences.zh: 曾復命，欲發其罪，致疏於袖中，累日未果言。

translations.literal: Ceng returned to report, wished to expose his crime, put a memorial in his sleeve, and for many days failed to speak.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Ceng meant to report the man's misconduct and kept a memorial in his sleeve, but for days could not bring himself to speak.

sentences.zh: 小將恐事泄，先誣告曾使酒，幾敗軍事，劉捍因證之，由是罷職，歸於齊之別墅。

translations.literal: The minor general feared exposure, first falsely accused Ceng of being drunk on duty, nearly ruining military affairs; Liu Kan bore witness; thereby he was dismissed and returned to a suburban villa in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The officer, fearing exposure, accused Ceng first of drunkenness on duty and nearly wrecked the mission; Liu Kan backed the charge; Ceng was dismissed and retired to a villa in Qi.

sentences.zh: 俄而王師範起兵叛，太祖促召曾，謂之曰：「子能緩頰說青州使無背盟，吾不負子矣。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Shifan raised troops in rebellion; the Founder urgently summoned Ceng and said: "If you can soothe Qingzhou and keep them from breaking the alliance, I will not fail you.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Shifan rebelled; the Founder urgently summoned Ceng and said, "If you can persuade Qingzhou not to break faith, I will not fail you.

sentences.zh: 」曾持檄以往。

translations.literal: " Ceng took the proclamation and went.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng took the edict and set out.

sentences.zh: 既至青，師範囚之，送於淮南，遇害。

translations.literal: Once he reached Qing, Shifan imprisoned him and sent him to Huainan, where he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingzhou Shifan imprisoned him and sent him to Huainan, where he was killed.

sentences.zh: 後太祖暴師範之罪曰：「喪我骨肉，殺我賓僚。

translations.literal: Later the Founder exposed Shifan's crimes, saying: "He bereaved my flesh and bone, killed my guest officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Founder denounced Shifan's crimes, saying, "He destroyed my kin and slew my retainers.

sentences.zh: 」遂族誅之。

translations.literal: " He then executed his whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then exterminated Shifan's clan.

sentences.zh: 因召曾二子，皆授以官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Ceng's two sons and both gave them office.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Ceng's two sons and gave them both posts.

sentences.zh: 孫騭，滑台人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhi, a man of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhi came from Huatai.

sentences.zh: 嗜學知書，微有辭筆。

translations.literal: Fond of learning, knew books, and had slight literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, was well read, and had some skill with the pen.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟中，魏博從事公乘億以女妻之，因教以箋奏程式。

translations.literal: In Tang Guangqi, Weibo staff officer Gongcheng Yi gave him his daughter in marriage and thereby taught him the forms of memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi, Weibo staff officer Gongcheng Yi gave him his daughter in marriage and taught him the forms of memorials and reports.

sentences.zh: 時中原多難，文章之士，縮影竄跡不自顯。

translations.literal: At the time the central plains had many troubles; men of letters shrank their shadows, hid their tracks, and did not display themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The central plains were in turmoil; men of letters hid themselves and did not seek notice.

sentences.zh: 億既死，魏帥以章表箋疏淹積，兼月不能發一字，或以騭為言，即署本職，主奏記事。

translations.literal: After Yi died the Wei commander had memorials, reports, letters and memos piled up; for a month and more not a word could be sent; someone spoke of Zhi, and he was at once given his proper post, in charge of memorial writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died the Wei commander's desk was buried in memorials for more than a month with no reply sent; when Zhi was recommended he was put in charge of drafting at once.

sentences.zh: 累遷職自支使、掌記至節度判官；

translations.literal: He rose through posts from branch commissioner, chief recorder, to circuit judicial commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: He rose from branch commissioner and chief recorder to circuit judicial commissioner;

sentences.zh: 奏官自校書、御史郎官、中丞、檢校常侍至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: and through presented offices from collating clerk, censor, bureau director, acting regular attendant, to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: and through presented ranks from collating clerk and censor to bureau director, acting regular attendant, and Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 太祖禦天下，念潛龍時，騭奉其主，好問往來數十返，甚錄之。

translations.literal: The Founder ruled the realm, recalled his hidden-dragon days when Zhi served his lord, good questions going back and forth several tens of times, and greatly recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder ruled the realm he remembered how Zhi had served him in his rise, their letters going back and forth dozens of times, and valued it highly.

sentences.zh: 開平三年，除右諫議大夫，滿歲，遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Kaiping year 3 he was made Right Remonstrance Grand Master; at term's end he was transferred to Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 3 he became Right Remonstrance Grand Master; after a year he was made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.

sentences.zh: 騭雅好聚書，有《六經》、漢史洎百家之言，凡數千卷，皆簡翰精至，披勘詳定，得暇即朝夕耽玩，曾無少怠。

translations.literal: Zhi especially loved collecting books; he had the 《Six Classics》, Han histories, and the masters' words, in all several thousand scrolls, all script refined and examined in detail; when he had leisure he devoured them morning and evening without the slightest slack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi loved books; he owned several thousand scrolls of the 《Six Classics》, Han histories, and the masters, all finely copied and collated, and whenever he had a moment he read morning and night without slack.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年春，太祖將議北巡，選朝士三十餘人扈從。

translations.literal: In the spring of Qianhua year 2 the Founder was to deliberate a northern tour and chose more than thirty court officers to attend in escort.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianhua 2 the Founder planned a northern tour and chose more than thirty court officers to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 二月甲子，車駕發自洛陽。

translations.literal: Second month, day jiazi, the imperial carriage set out from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the second month the imperial carriage left Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 禺中，次白馬頓，召文武官就食，以從臣未集，駐蹕以俟之；

translations.literal: At the fifth watch they halted at Baima post, summoned civil and military officers to eat; because the following ministers were not assembled, the procession halted to wait;
translations.idiomatic: At midmorning they stopped at Baima post and called the civil and military officers to eat; the escort had not all arrived, so the procession waited;

sentences.zh: 又命飛騎促於道，而騭與諫議大夫張衍、兵部郎中張俊等累刻方至，太祖性本卞急，因茲大怒，並格殺於前墀。

translations.literal: and again ordered flying riders to hurry them on the road, but Zhi, Remonstrance Grand Master Zhang Yan, Bureau Director in the Ministry of War Zhang Jun and others, after many quarter-hours only then arrived; the Founder's nature was originally brusque and quick-tempered; thereby he was greatly angry and all were beaten to death on the front courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: couriers were sent to hurry stragglers on the road, but Zhi, Remonstrance Grand Master Zhang Yan, Bureau Director Zhang Jun, and others arrived only after long delay; the Founder was by nature irascible, flew into a rage, and had them all beaten to death in the forecourt.

sentences.zh: 張俊，字彥臣。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, style Yanchen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, styled Yanchen.

sentences.zh: 祖、父咸有聞於時。

translations.literal: Grandfather and father both had repute in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Both his grandfather and father were known in their day.

sentences.zh: 俊少孤，自修飾，善為五言詩，其警句頗為人所稱。

translations.literal: Jun was orphaned young, self-cultivated in deportment, skilled at five-character verse; his striking lines were often praised by men.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he cultivated himself, wrote fine five-character verse, and his striking lines won praise.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明中，黃巢犯京師，天子幸蜀，士皆竄伏窟穴，以保其生。

translations.literal: In Tang Guangming, Huang Chao violated the capital; the Son of Heaven went to Shu; scholars all hid in holes and caves to preserve their lives.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangming Huang Chao took the capital; the emperor fled to Shu; scholars hid wherever they could to survive.

sentences.zh: 俊亦晦跡浮泛，不失其道。

translations.literal: Jun also concealed his tracks and drifted, not losing his way.
translations.idiomatic: Jun too kept out of sight and drifted, yet never abandoned his principles.

sentences.zh: 及僖宗還京師，由校書郎、西畿尉登朝為御史、補闕、起居郎、司勳員外、萬年縣令，以事黜官峽中，將十年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital he rose from collating clerk and western capital district magistrate to court as censor, supplementation official, director of attendance, acting director in the Bureau of Merit, and Wan'ian county magistrate; for an affair he was dismissed to the gorges of the Three Gorges, nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong returned he rose from collating clerk and western capital district magistrate to censor, supplementation official, attendance director, acting director in the Bureau of Merit, and magistrate of Wan'ian; an offense sent him into exile in the gorges for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，用宰臣薛貽矩為鹽鐵使，俊與貽矩同年登第，甚知其才，即奏為鹽鐵判官，遷職為禮部郎中，兼職如故。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne he used chief minister Xue Yiju as salt and iron commissioner; Jun and Yiju had passed the examination in the same year and well knew his talent; he at once memorialized Jun as salt and iron judicial commissioner, promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites, concurrent post as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne chief minister Xue Yiju became salt and iron commissioner; Jun had passed the jinshi with Yiju and knew his ability; he was soon made salt and iron judicial commissioner, then Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites while keeping the same concurrent duties.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年二月，扈從後至，與孫騭、張衍同日遇禍於白馬頓。

translations.literal: Qianhua year 2 second month, he came late in escort and with Sun Zhi and Zhang Yan on the same day met disaster at Baima post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qianhua 2 he came late on the northern tour and, with Sun Zhi and Zhang Yan, was killed the same day at Baima post.

sentences.zh: 張衍，字元用，河南尹魏王宗奭之猶子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan, style Yuanyong, was a nephew of Henan prefect and Prince of Wei Zong Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, styled Yuanyong, was a nephew of Henan prefect and Prince of Wei Zong Shi.

sentences.zh: 其父死於兵間。

translations.literal: His father died amid war.
translations.idiomatic: His father had died in the wars.

sentences.zh: 衍樂讀書為儒，始以經學就舉，不中選。

translations.literal: Yan delighted in reading books as a classicist; at first with classical learning he took the examination but was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: Yan loved the classics and first tried the civil service examination on classical learning but failed.

sentences.zh: 時諫議大夫鄭徽退居洛陽，以女妻之，遂令應辭科，不數上登第。

translations.literal: At the time Remonstrance Grand Master Zheng Hui retired to Luoyang, gave him his daughter in marriage, and then had him take the literary examination; in not many attempts he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grand Master Zheng Hui, retired in Luoyang, gave him his daughter and had him try the literary examination; he passed after only a few attempts.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗東遷，以宗奭勳力隆峻，衍由校書郎拜左拾遺，旋召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhaozong moved east, because Zong Shi's merit was lofty and weighty, Yan from collating clerk was appointed Left Collector and Memorialist, and soon summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved east, on Zong Shi's great merit Yan rose from collating clerk to Left Collector and Memorialist and was soon made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，罷之，特拜考功郎中，俄遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne he was dismissed, specially appointed Acting Director of Examination in the inner rank, and soon transferred to Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne Yan was removed from the Hanlin post, made Acting Director of Examination, and soon Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 衍巧生業，樂積聚。

translations.literal: Yan was clever at making a living and delighted in accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was shrewd at profit and loved to hoard wealth.

sentences.zh: 太祖將北伐，頗以扈從間糜耗力用係意，屢幹托宰執求免是行；

translations.literal: The Founder was about to campaign north; he greatly tied his mind to the waste of effort in escort service; repeatedly pleaded with the chief executives to be excused from this journey;
translations.idiomatic: As the Founder prepared a northern campaign Yan dreaded the cost of escort duty and repeatedly asked the chief ministers to excuse him from the journey;

sentences.zh: 太祖微聞之，又屬應召稽晚，與孫騭等同日遇禍。

translations.literal: the Founder slightly heard of it, and again as he was slow in answering the summons, with Sun Zhi and the rest he met disaster on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: the Founder caught wind of it; when Yan was also slow to answer the summons he suffered the same fate as Sun Zhi that day.

sentences.zh: 杜荀鶴，池州人。

translations.literal: Du Xunhe, a man of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xunhe came from Chizhou.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （辛文房《唐才子傳》：荀鶴，字彥之，牧之微子也。）〉

translations.literal: (Xin Wenfang's 《Records of Tang Talents》: Xunhe, style Yanzhi, was a minor son of Muzhi.)
translations.idiomatic: (Xin Wenfang's 《Records of Tang Talents》 says Xunhe, styled Yanzhi, was an illegitimate son of Du Mu.)

sentences.zh: 善為詩，辭句切理，為時所許。

translations.literal: Skilled at poetry, his phrases cut to reason, approved by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry with phrases that cut to the point and won contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 既擢第，復還舊山。

translations.literal: Having passed the examination he returned again to his old mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi he went back to his old home in the hills.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《唐才子傳》：荀鶴嘗謁梁王朱全忠，與之坐，忽無雲而雨，王以為天泣不祥，命作詩，稱意，王喜之。

translations.literal: (The 《Records of Tang Talents》 says: Xunhe once called on Prince of Liang Zhu Quanzhong and sat with him; suddenly rain fell from a cloudless sky; the prince thought heaven wept—an ill omen—and ordered him to compose a poem; it pleased him and the prince was delighted.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Records of Tang Talents》 records that Xunhe once visited Prince of Liang Zhu Quanzhong; as they sat together rain fell though the sky was clear; the prince took it as heaven weeping and ordered a poem; pleased with it, he was delighted.

sentences.zh: 荀鶴寒進，連敗文場，甚苦，至是送春官。

translations.literal: Xunhe came up poor, failed repeatedly in the literary arena, suffered greatly, and only then was sent to the spring office.
translations.idiomatic: Xunhe had come up in poverty, failed again and again in the examinations, and suffered greatly before he was finally sent to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大順二年，裴贄侍郎放第八人登科，正月十日放榜，正荀鶴生朝也。

translations.literal: In Dazhun year 2 Vice Minister Pei Zan released the eighth man on the rolls; on the tenth day of the first month the list was posted—exactly Xunhe's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhun 2 Vice Minister Pei Zan placed him eighth on the list; the roster was posted on the tenth day of the first month—Xunhe's own birthday.

sentences.zh: 王希羽獻詩曰：「金榜曉懸生世日，玉書潛記上升時。

translations.literal: Wang Xiyu presented a poem saying: "At dawn the golden list hangs on the day of his birth; the jade record secretly notes the hour of his ascent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiyu offered a poem: "At dawn the golden list marks the day of his birth; the jade register secretly records the hour of his rise.

sentences.zh: 九華山色高千尺，未必高於第八枝。

translations.literal: Mount Jiuhua's color rises a thousand feet—yet may not be higher than the eighth branch."
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jiuhua stands a thousand feet high—yet hardly towers above the eighth place on the list."

sentences.zh: 」又，《唐新纂》云：荀鶴舉進士及第，東歸，過夷門，獻梁太祖詩句云：「四海九州空第一，不同諸鎮府封王。

translations.literal: " Further, the 《Tang New Compilation》 says: Xunhe passed the jinshi examination, returned east, passed Yimen, and presented lines to the Liang Founder: "Alone first through the four seas and nine provinces—unlike the various governors enfeoffed as kings.
translations.idiomatic: " The 《Tang New Compilation》 adds: Xunhe took his jinshi degree, went east, passed Yimen, and gave the Liang Founder this verse: "First in all the realm—unlike the warlords made kings of their circuits.

sentences.zh: 」是則荀鶴之受知於梁祖舊矣，不待田頵之箋問而始被遇也。）〉

translations.literal: " Thus Xunhe had long won the Liang Founder's notice and did not await Tian Yun's letter of inquiry before first being received.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " So the Liang Founder had known Xunhe long before Tian Yun's letter brought him to court.)〉

sentences.zh: 時田頵在宣州，甚重之。

translations.literal: At that time Tian Yun was at Xuanzhou and valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun was then at Xuanzhou and held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 頵將起兵，乃陰令以箋問至，太祖遇之頗厚。

translations.literal: When Yun was about to raise troops he secretly sent a letter of inquiry; the Founder received him quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun prepared to rebel he secretly sent a letter of inquiry ahead; the Founder treated Xunhe very well.

sentences.zh: 及頵遇禍，太祖以其才表之，尋授翰林學士、主客員外郎。

translations.literal: When Yun met disaster the Founder memorialized on his talent and soon made him Hanlin academician and Supernumerary Vice Director in the Ministry of Reception for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun's fall the Founder praised his talent at court and soon made him Hanlin academician and supernumerary vice director of the Ministry of Reception.

sentences.zh: 既而恃太祖之勢，凡搢紳間己所不悅者，日屈指怒數，將謀盡殺之。

translations.literal: Before long, relying on the Founder's power, among the gentry anyone he disliked he would daily count on his fingers in anger, plotting to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, trusting in the Founder's favor, he daily counted on his fingers the courtiers he hated and plotted to kill them all.

sentences.zh: 苞蓄未及泄丁重疾，旬日而卒。

translations.literal: His hoarded spite had not yet been vented when he fell gravely ill and died within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: His grudges had not yet been acted on when he fell gravely ill and died within ten days.

sentences.zh: 羅隱，

translations.literal: Luo Yin,
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yin,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《唐才子傳》：隱字昭諫。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 says: Yin, style Zhaojian.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 gives his style as Zhaojian.)〉

sentences.zh: 餘杭人。

translations.literal: a native of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: was from Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 詩名於天下，尤長於詠史，然多所譏諷，以故不中第，大為唐宰相鄭畋、李蔚所知。

translations.literal: His poetry was famed throughout the realm; he was especially adept at historical verse, yet often satirical, and for that reason never passed the examinations—though greatly esteemed by Tang chancellors Zheng Tian and Li Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His verse was known everywhere; he excelled at historical poems but often mocked his betters, failed the examinations for it, and was nevertheless prized by chancellors Zheng Tian and Li Wei.

sentences.zh: 隱雖負文稱，然貌古而陋。

translations.literal: Though Yin bore a literary reputation, his appearance was archaic and uncomely.
translations.idiomatic: For all his literary fame, Yin looked old and plain.

sentences.zh: 畋女幼有文性，嘗覽隱詩卷，諷誦不已，畋疑其女有慕才之意。

translations.literal: Tian's daughter had literary gifts from youth; once reading Yin's poetry she recited it endlessly, and Tian suspected she admired the man's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's daughter was literary; reading Yin's poems she could not stop reciting them, and Tian thought she admired the poet.

sentences.zh: 一日，隱至第，鄭女垂簾而窺之，自是絕不詠其詩。

translations.literal: One day Yin came to the mansion; the Zheng girl peered through a lowered curtain—after that she never chanted his poems again.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin visited the house the girl peeked through the curtain; from then on she never read his verse again.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明中，因亂歸鄉里，節度使錢鏐辟為從事。

translations.literal: In Tang's Guangming era, owing to disorder he returned home; military commissioner Qian Liu engaged him as staff.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangming he went home in the turmoil; Qian Liu of Zhexi took him on as staff.

sentences.zh: 開平初，太祖以右諫議大夫征，不至。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiping the Founder summoned him as Right Remonstrance Counselor; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiping the Founder called him to court as Right Remonstrance Counselor; he refused.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使羅紹威密表推薦，乃授給事中。

translations.literal: Wei-Bo military commissioner Luo Shaowei secretly memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei of Wei-Bo secretly recommended him, and he was made Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，終於錢塘。

translations.literal: Over eighty years old, he died at Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He was over eighty when he died at Qiantang.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《澗泉日記》云：唐光啟三年，吳越王表奏為錢塘令，遷著作郎，辟掌書記。

translations.literal: (The 《Jianquan Diary》 says: In Tang Guangqi 3 the King of Wuyue memorialized him as magistrate of Qiantang, promoted him to Drafting Gentleman, and engaged him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Jianquan Diary》 says: In Guangqi 3 the King of Wuyue had him made magistrate of Qiantang, then drafting gentleman and chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，充判官。

translations.literal: In Tianyou 3 he served as judge-adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 he was a judge-adviser.

sentences.zh: 梁開平二年，授給事中。

translations.literal: In Liang Kaiping 2 he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 2 of Liang he became Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷發運使。

translations.literal: Year 3 he was transferred to grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是年卒，葬於定山鄉。

translations.literal: That year he died and was buried in Dingshan township.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year and was buried in Dingshan township.

sentences.zh: 金部郎中沈崧銘其墓。）〉

translations.literal: Revenue-department cadre Shen Song inscribed his tomb.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shen Song of the Revenue Department wrote his tomb inscription.)〉

sentences.zh: 有文集數卷行於世。

translations.literal: Several fascicles of collected works circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Several fascicles of his collected works still circulate.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《唐才子傳》云：隱所著《讒書》、《讒本》、《淮海寓言》、《湘南應用集》、《甲乙集》、外集啟事等，並行於世。

translations.literal: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 says: Yin's works—the 《Book of Satire》, 《Satire Originals》, 《Parables of Huaihai》, 《Applied Collection of Xiangnan》, 《Jia-yi Collection》, outer collections of memorials and the like—all circulate.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 lists his 《Book of Satire》, 《Satire Originals》, 《Parables of Huaihai》, 《Applied Collection of Xiangnan》, 《Jia-yi Collection》, memorial collections, and other works in circulation.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：羅隱在科場，恃才傲物，尤為公卿所惡，故六舉不第。

translations.literal: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Luo Yin in the examination field, relying on talent and arrogant toward others, was especially hated by court nobles, and thus failed six times.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: In the examinations Yin leaned on his talent, was proud and rude, and was so hated by the great families that he failed six times.

sentences.zh: 時長安有羅尊師者，深於相術，隱以貌陋，恐為相術所棄，每與尊師接談，常自大以沮之。

translations.literal: At that time in Chang'an there was Master Luo, deep in physiognomy; Yin, fearing his ugly looks would be rejected by the art, whenever he talked with the master would boast greatly to put him off.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an there was a Master Luo skilled in physiognomy; Yin, fearing his looks would doom him, always bragged when they met to discourage a reading.

sentences.zh: 及其累遭黜落，不得已始往問焉。

translations.literal: After repeated failures he had no choice and at last went to ask.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated failures he finally went to ask his fortune.

sentences.zh: 尊師笑曰：「貧道知之久矣，但以吾子決在一第，未可與語。

translations.literal: The master laughed and said: "This poor Taoist has known long—but your fate is fixed at a single jinshi pass, and I could not yet speak with you.
translations.idiomatic: The master laughed: "I have known you long—but you are fated for only one jinshi success, and until now I could not tell you.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，貧道敢有所隱乎！

translations.literal: Today's matter—can this poor Taoist still hide anything!
translations.idiomatic: Today I dare hide nothing from you!

sentences.zh: 且吾子之於一第也，貧道觀之，雖首冠群英，亦不過簿尉爾。

translations.literal: As for your jinshi, this poor Taoist sees that even were you first among all the gifted, you would rise no higher than registrar or sheriff.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you topped the jinshi list, I see you rising no higher than a county clerk or sheriff.

sentences.zh: 若能罷舉，東歸霸國以求用，則必富且貴矣。

translations.literal: If you can abandon the examinations, return east to the hegemon's state and seek employment, then you will surely be rich and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Quit the examinations, go east to the hegemon's court, and you will grow rich and honored.

sentences.zh: 兩途，吾子宜自擇之。

translations.literal: Two roads—my son, choose for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Two paths—choose between them."

sentences.zh: 」隱懵然不知所措者數日。

translations.literal: Yin was dazed and for several days did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was stunned and for days could not decide.

sentences.zh: 鄰居有賣飯媼，見隱驚曰：「何辭色之沮喪如此，莫有不決之事否？

translations.literal: A neighbor who sold meals, seeing Yin's dismay, said in surprise: "Why such a downcast look—surely something is unresolved?
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor who sold meals saw his gloom and said: "Why so wretched—something you cannot decide?

sentences.zh: 」隱謂知之，因盡以尊師之言告之。

translations.literal: Yin thought she understood and told her the master's words in full.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking she might understand, he told her everything the master had said.

sentences.zh: 媼歎曰：「秀才何自迷甚焉，且天下皆知羅隱，何須一第然後為得哉！

translations.literal: The old woman sighed: "Scholar, how deeply you mislead yourself! All the world knows Luo Yin—why must a jinshi degree be the only way to succeed!
translations.idiomatic: She sighed: "Scholar, you fool yourself! Everyone knows Luo Yin—why must a degree be your only success?

sentences.zh: 不如急取富貴，則老婆之願也。

translations.literal: Better hurry to wealth and rank—that is this old woman's wish."
translations.idiomatic: Take wealth and office now—that is what I wish for you."

sentences.zh: 」隱聞之釋然，遂歸錢塘。

translations.literal: Hearing this Yin felt relieved and at once returned to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Relieved, he went straight back to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 時錢鏐方得兩浙，置之幕府，使典軍中書檄，其後官給事中。

translations.literal: Qian Liu had just secured the two Zhes; he placed Yin in his staff to draft military documents, and afterward made him Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu had just taken the two Zhes; he put Yin in his secretariat to draft army papers and later made him Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 初，隱罷上中書之日，費窘，因抵魏謁鄴王羅紹威，將入其境，先貽書敘其家世，鄴王為侄。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yin left the capital after failing the Secretariat examination, he was in straits; he therefore went to Wei to visit Prince Luo Shaowei and, before entering his territory, sent a letter stating their family kinship—the prince was his nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Once, broke after failing the Secretariat exam, he went to Wei to see Luo Shaowei and beforehand sent a letter claiming kinship—the prince was his nephew.

sentences.zh: 幕府僚吏見其書，皆怒曰：「羅隱一布衣爾，而侄視大王，其可乎！

translations.literal: Staff officers who saw the letter all said in anger: "Luo Yin is only a commoner—yet he treats the king as nephew! How can that be!
translations.idiomatic: His staff read the letter and cried: "Luo Yin is a nobody—yet he calls the prince his nephew! Impossible!

sentences.zh: 」紹威素重士，且曰：「羅隱名振天下，王公大夫多為所薄，今惠然肯顧，其何以勝！

translations.literal: Shaowei had always valued scholars and said: "Luo Yin's name shakes the world; many lords and grandees he has belittled—now that he willingly comes, how can I not be overcome!
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei, who loved scholars, said: "Luo Yin's name fills the realm; lords and ministers he has often scorned—now he honors me—how can I not be overwhelmed!

sentences.zh: 得在侄行，為幸多矣，敢不致恭，諸公慎勿言。

translations.literal: To stand in the nephew's place is already great fortune; how dare I not show respect—gentlemen, say no more."
translations.idiomatic: To receive him as a nephew is already my luck; I dare not be cold—say nothing, gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 」於是擁旆郊迎，一見即拜，隱亦不讓。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went with banners to welcome him at the suburbs; at first sight he bowed, and Yin did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: He went out with banners to meet him at the suburbs, bowed at once, and Yin accepted without demur.

sentences.zh: 及將行，紹威贈以百萬，他物稱是，仍致書於鏐謂叔父，鏐首用之。）〉

translations.literal: When Yin was about to leave, Shaowei gave him a million in cash and gifts in proportion, and also wrote Qian Liu calling him uncle—Liu employed him from the first.)〉
translations.idiomatic: On his departure Shaowei gave him a million cash and rich gifts, and wrote Qian Liu as to an uncle—Liu took him up at once.)〉

sentences.zh: 仇殷，不知何郡人也。

translations.literal: Chou Yin—of what commandery he came is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Yin came from a commandery that is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 開平中，仕至欽天監，明於象緯曆數，藝術精密，近無其比。

translations.literal: In Kaiping he rose to Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, skilled in the constellations, calendrical reckoning, and the arts; in precision none of his day could compare.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping he reached Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, master of stars, calendars, and divination, unrivaled in his generation.

sentences.zh: 光化中，太祖在滑，遣密王友倫以兵三萬禦幽州之師十餘萬，深慮其不敵，召殷問曰：「陣可行乎？

translations.literal: In Guanghua, when the Founder was at Hua, he secretly sent Prince of Mi Wang Youlun with thirty thousand men against a Youzhou host of more than a hundred thousand; deeply fearing they could not prevail, he summoned Yin and asked: "Can battle lines be formed?
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghua, at Hua, the Founder secretly sent Prince of Mi Wang Youlun with thirty thousand men against more than a hundred thousand from Youzhou; fearing defeat, he asked Yin: "Can we give battle?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「其十四日過禺中乎！

translations.literal: He said: "On the fourteenth they will pass the mid-morning hour!
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "On the fourteenth they will pass mid-morning!

sentences.zh: 」又問之，曰：「賊敗塗地。

translations.literal: Asked again, he said: "The rebels will be crushed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Asked again: "The enemy will be routed.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「既望，當見捷書。

translations.literal: He also said: "On the day after the full moon you will see the victory report.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "On the sixteenth you will see the victory dispatch.

sentences.zh: 」果如其言，不失晷刻。

translations.literal: It happened exactly as he said, not missing a moment on the sundial.
translations.idiomatic: Events matched his words to the very hour.

sentences.zh: 太祖之在長蘆也，諸將請攻壁，號令軍中，人負槁二圍，置千積，俄而雲集。

translations.literal: When the Founder was at Changlu the generals asked to assault the walls; he ordered the army that each man carry two armfuls of fodder and set a thousand stacks—soon they piled like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: At Changlu the generals urged an assault; the Founder ordered every soldier to carry two bundles of straw and pile a thousand stacks, which soon rose like clouds.

sentences.zh: 殷曰：「何用？

translations.literal: Yin said: "What use?
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "What is the use?

sentences.zh: 」或以所謀告之，殷曰：「我占矣，不見攻壁象，無乃自退乎！

translations.literal: When they told him the plan, Yin said: "I have divined—there is no sign of assaulting walls; will they not withdraw of themselves!
translations.idiomatic: Told the plan, Yin said: "I have cast the signs—no image of storming walls; they will retreat on their own!

sentences.zh: 」翌日，有騎馳報丁會以潞州叛，太祖令盡焚其槁而還，不克攻。

translations.literal: The next day a rider galloped in reporting that Ding Hui had rebelled at Luzhou; the Founder ordered all the fodder burned and returned, and the assault was not made.
translations.idiomatic: Next day a courier reported Ding Hui's rebellion at Lu; the Founder had the straw burned and marched back without attacking.

sentences.zh: 開平中，殷一日朝罷，過崇政院，使敬翔直閣，翔問之曰：「月犯房次星，其逼若綴，是何祥也？

translations.literal: In Kaiping, one day after court Yin passed the Chongzheng Court and had Attendant Jing Xiang on duty; Xiang asked him: "The moon trespasses on a star in the Fang mansion—the approach seems drawn out; what omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping, leaving court one day Yin passed the Chongzheng Court where Jing Xiang was on duty; Xiang asked: "The moon encroaches on a star in Fang—the approach looks slow; what omen is this?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「常度耳。

translations.literal: He said: "A routine measure."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "Nothing unusual."

sentences.zh: 」殷欲不言，既過數步，自度不可默，乃反言曰：「三兩日當有不順語至，無或驟恐，宜先白上知。

translations.literal: Yin wished not to speak; having gone several paces he reckoned he could not keep silent, turned back and said: "In two or three days ill news will arrive—do not panic suddenly; you should first inform His Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: He meant to say nothing; after a few steps he turned back: "In two or three days bad news will come—do not be alarmed; tell the Emperor first."

sentences.zh: 」既二日，陝府奏同州劉知俊閉關作叛。

translations.literal: Two days later Shaanxi memorialized that Tongzhou's Liu Zhijun had closed the passes and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Shaanxi reported that Liu Zhijun of Tong had shut the passes and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 初，王景仁之出師也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Jingren marched out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Jingren took the field.

sentences.zh: 殷上言：「太陰虧，不利深入。

translations.literal: Yin memorialized: "The yin moon is deficient—deep advance is ill-omened."
translations.idiomatic: Yin warned: "The moon is waning—deep advance is unlucky."

sentences.zh: 」太祖遽遣使止之，已敗於柏鄉矣。

translations.literal: The Founder hastily sent an envoy to stop him, but he had already been defeated at Baixiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder hurriedly sent orders to halt him, but Jingren had already been beaten at Baixiang.

sentences.zh: 殷所見觸類如是，不可備錄。

translations.literal: Yin's divinations of this sort cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Cases like these fill his record and cannot all be given here.

sentences.zh: 然而畏慎特甚，居常寢默，未嘗敢顯言。

translations.literal: Yet he was exceedingly timid; he usually slept in silence and never dared speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was deeply cautious, usually kept silent, and never dared speak openly.

sentences.zh: 縱言事跡，惟其語音，不可盡曉，以故屢貽責罰。

translations.literal: Even when he spoke of events, only his speech—none could fully understand—and for that he was repeatedly fined and punished.
translations.idiomatic: When he did speak, his accent made him hard to understand, and he was often fined for it.

sentences.zh: 後卒於官。

translations.literal: Later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office.

sentences.zh: 段深，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Duan Shen—of what place he came is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shen came from a place that is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 開平中，以善醫待詔於翰林。

translations.literal: In Kaiping, for skill in medicine he attended at court in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping, as a skilled physician, he served in the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 時太祖抱疾久之，其溲甚濁，僧曉微侍藥有征，賜紫衣師號，錫賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The Founder had long been ill; his urine was very turbid; the monk Xiaowei attended with medicine that took effect, and he was given purple robes, a master's title, and very rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder had been ill a long time with foul urine; the monk Xiaowei treated him with success and received purple robes, a master's title, and lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 頃之疾發，曉微剝服色，去師號。

translations.literal: Soon the illness flared again; Xiaowei was stripped of his robes and title.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness returned, Xiaowei lost his robes and title.

sentences.zh: 因召深問曰：「疾愈復作，草藥不足恃也，我左右粒石而效者眾矣，服之如何？

translations.literal: The Founder then summoned Shen and asked: "The illness eased and has returned—herbs are not to be relied on; many around me have taken powdered stone with effect—how would it be to take it?
translations.idiomatic: The Founder called Shen and asked: "I improved and relapsed—herbs are not enough; many at court swear by powdered stone—should I take it?

sentences.zh: 」深對曰：「臣嘗奉詔診切，陛下積憂勤，失調護，脈代芤而心益虛。

translations.literal: Shen replied: "Your servant has examined Your Majesty by imperial order; Your Majesty has accumulated worry and toil, lost proper care, the pulse is hollow in succession and the heart grows ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Shen answered: "When I examined Your Majesty by order, I found long worry and overwork, poor care, a hollow pulse, and a weakening heart.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜先治心，心和平而溲變清，當進飲劑，而不當粒石也。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks the heart should be treated first; when the heart is calm the urine will clear—decoctions should be given, not powdered stone."
translations.idiomatic: Treat the heart first; when the heart is calm the urine will clear—give decoctions, not powdered stone."

sentences.zh: 臣謹案，《太倉公傳》曰：『中熱不溲者不可服石，石性精悍，有大毒。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes that the 《Biography of the Granary Lord》 says: "One who has internal heat and cannot urinate must not take stone; stone is keen and fierce and greatly toxic.
translations.idiomatic: I cite the 《Biography of the Granary Lord》: "Internal heat with no urine forbids stone medicine; stone is sharp, fierce, and highly toxic.

sentences.zh: 』凡餌毒藥如甲兵，不得已而用之，非有危殆，不可服也。

translations.literal: All taking poisonous drugs is like deploying armor—use them only when there is no choice; without grave danger they must not be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Poisonous drugs are like arms—use them only when there is no other way; without mortal danger, do not take them."

sentences.zh: 」太祖善之，令進飲劑，疾稍愈，乃以幣帛賜之。

translations.literal: The Founder approved, ordered decoctions given, the illness eased somewhat, and then bestowed silks on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder agreed, took decoctions, improved somewhat, and rewarded him with silks.
